sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Local database service
sections.what: Starts a PostgreSQL 16 database with a fixed user, password and database name, makes port 5432 reachable from the machine, keeps data in a saved volume, and checks the database is responding.
sections.why: Likely reason: every developer and test run uses the same database.
sections.watch_out: The port is published on all network interfaces, so the fixed password can be reached from other machines on the same network.

summary: Defines a local PostgreSQL 16 database that runs in a container for development and testing.
purpose: Give everyone the same database setup without installing one by hand.
why: Likely reason: a shared container gives consistent results. The .env.example comment says its settings match this file.
how: 1) Docker starts the database container. 2) It creates the user, password and database with the given names. 3) It keeps data in a named volume. 4) A health check waits until the database responds.
inputs: Fixed values written in the file; nothing is typed in.
outputs: A running database listening on port 5432.
risks: The fixed password and open port are fine on a personal machine but not on a shared network. Deleting the volume erases the data.
debug: If the app cannot connect, check the container is healthy and the port is not used by another database. If data disappears, check the volume was not removed.
